bioAdditions: A 'Daniel Scott Jr.' headed a household in Pittston Township in 1810: a man aged 26-44, a woman aged 16-25 and three young children, two of them boys (S1). The man's age fits the tree's birth year of 1778 (and rules out FamilySearch's 1788, since he would then have been 22), and the young wife fits Hannah Devens (b. 1787). The 'Jr.' implies an older Daniel Scott in the same area; a Daniel Scott appears among the 1796 taxables of neighbouring Providence Township (S2). A Joseph Scott and a Stephen Scott (aged 16-25) were enumerated on the same Pittston page (S1). This is consistent with, but does not prove, the FamilySearch claim that Daniel and Hannah (Devens) Scott were the parents of Stephen J. Scott (b. Feb 1806). The FamilySearch profile makes him a son of Matthew Scott of Bennington, Vermont (d. 1789); the 'Jr.' in 1810 sits awkwardly with that, unless 'Jr.' distinguished him from an unrelated older Daniel.

conflicts.assessment: 1810 census supports the tree's 1778 over FamilySearch's 1788 (if this is the right man).

relationships.evidence: FamilySearch tree only; 1810 household shape fits

openQuestionsNew: Who was 'Daniel Scott' (Sr.) of Providence Twp (1796 taxable) - the father of Daniel Jr., rather than Matthew Scott of Vermont?
Did Daniel die c.1811 (FS) and did Hannah remarry a Covert (Find a Grave index 'Hannah Devens Covert'; Coverts lived in Plymouth Twp in 1840)?
